item.title: U.S. Marines Cancel Drill With South Korea, Citing Iran War Demands
item.description: The move to call off the high-profile event was communicated in June, South Korea said. President Trump shortened another joint military exercise earlier this month.

item.title: Four Years Ago, a Crypto Boss Went Missing. Now His Successor Has.
item.description: The mysterious collapse of a European cryptocurrency exchange helps to explain why the industry hasn’t shaken off its reputation as a magnet for criminals.

item.title: Iran Warns Gulf States Not to Join Trump’s Economic War
item.description: Iran’s new hard-line national security adviser, Mohsen Rezaei, vowed to prevent “a single drop of oil” from leaving the region.

item.title: Where Iran’s Young People Gather, the Government Sees Threats to Its Authority
item.description: In recent weeks, the police have closed dozens of cafes, often citing laws that stipulate women must veil in public. Experts say the closures are part of an effort to control public space.

item.title: Iran Pledges to Defy Trump’s Economic Sanctions
item.description: Analysts say Tehran could intensify the dispute militarily after attempts to squeeze its economy. An Iranian official vowed “not a single drop of oil” would leave the Gulf.

item.title: Syria and Israel Hold U.S.-Mediated Talks to Try to Ease Tensions
item.description: The discussions, reported by the Syrian state news agency, came days after Israel struck an air base in Syria’s northwest, the latest in a series of military interventions.

item.title: Zelensky Says His Ex-Defense Minister Was Wrong to Call for Elections
item.description: The Ukrainian president repeated his long-held position that elections in the middle of war would tear his country apart.

item.title: A New Effort to Punish Iran
item.description: The Trump administration says it will try to cut the country off from the global economy by targeting its trading partners.

item.title: UK Prime Minister Burnham Arrives in Ukraine as Russia Amps Up Warnings
item.description: In his first foreign trip since taking office, the British prime minister pledged to stand by Kyiv despite new warnings of potential consequences.

item.title: Echoing Trump, Latin America’s Leaders Boost Allies Across Borders
item.description: With cheers, endorsements and insults for rivals and “wokismo,” a new crop of right-wing leaders are openly stepping into one another’s elections.
